name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male Levite mentioned in the book of Ezra. He is noted specifically as one of the Levites whom Ezra sent to Iddo, indicating a role in the post-exilic community restoration efforts. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution' and is a proper name found in Ezra 8:16. This meaning may reflect themes of restoration or recovery, which aligns with the context of the return from exile, though the name itself was not given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Meshullam as a descendant of Levi, establishing his Levitical heritage. Beyond this tribal connection, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance lies in his participation as a Levite sent by Ezra to Iddo, which highlights his involvement in the organized efforts to reestablish the worship and community life of Israel after the exile. His role underscores the importance of the Levites in supporting the spiritual renewal of the nation under God's guidance during this period.
